Architecture / Principle distillation

Human-Agent Principle Distillation

How a difficult run becomes a reusable principle, an executable change, and a new test of the agent’s understanding.

Human-Agent Principle Distillation is the development process Yannick uses to turn experience into explicit reasoning knowledge. The SRA agent executes and produces evidence. The human identifies a principle. A coding agent helps formalize and integrate it. Another run tests what the changed system can actually do.

The intended result is a principle that remains useful when the objects, appearance, or arrangement change. Its applicability must preserve the causal conditions that made it relevant. This is how a particular difficulty can enrich a broader structure of meaning.

Yannick Fontan · Episode 2

Three contributions to the development loop

The human, the coding agent, and the running SRA have distinct responsibilities. Their contributions meet around evidence from the environment.

ParticipantContribution
HumanInterpret the difficulty, identify the intended meaning, and assess whether a proposed principle expresses the right general distinction.
Coding agentLocate existing mechanisms, formalize the principle, connect it to the architecture, and help evaluate the implementation.
SRA agentSelect and execute reasoning operations during play, then expose the observations and outcomes needed to assess their use.
The process in Episode 2

Find the actual reasoning gap

A failed run does not always mean a missing principle. The failure may come from a technical defect, mistaken evidence, an unsuitable condition of use, or a broken connection between an investigation and its parent goal. Start by identifying where the expected causal chain stops working.

Ask what the agent was trying to establish, which premises supported its choice, what effect it expected, and what it observed. A principle can already exist yet never reach the workflow that needs it. Repairing that connection is different from adding more knowledge.

Principle applicability and integration requirements

Give the principle a usable form

The principle migration design specifies records that connect a statement to its premises, applicability, typed parameters, invariants, expected effects, falsifiers, workflows, and evidence. These details make the statement operational and delimit its scope.

QuestionWhat the record should provide
When does it apply?Observable or explicitly derived premises, roles, and conditions.
What does it justify?A conclusion, investigation, revision, or action under those conditions.
What must remain true?Invariants and conditions that dependent steps require.
What would defeat it?An observable falsifier or a known counterexample.
Where is it used?References to selection, execution, reconciliation, and evidence of actual use.

Episode 6 distinguishes the parts: an operator performs a transformation, a workflow organizes transformations over time, and a principle states why a step is justified. A workflow can apply several principles; one principle can guide several workflows.

Versioned principle recordsOperators, workflows, and principles · Episode 6

Example: preserving a prerequisite

Illustrative reasoning example

Suppose standing on a pad opens a gate. The agent leaves the pad and the gate closes. Repeating the same attempt cannot establish a lasting passage. The observation suggests that opening depends on continued occupancy.

The reusable principle concerns preservation: when a later action depends on a condition, the plan must keep that condition satisfied until the dependent action is complete. The particular pad and gate are participants in this instance of the relation.

A movable object might maintain occupancy while the agent crosses. That possibility needs evidence: the object must be movable into position, its presence must activate the pad, and the gate must remain open. The resulting composition must still be executed and checked.

Connect the principle to executable reasoning

Integration connects meaning, applicability, control, and computation. The principle migration design assigns these responsibilities to different layers.

LayerIntegration responsibility
LogosRepresent terms, common principles, epistemic distinctions, and falsifiers.
DRMDeclare applicability, roles, goals, variants, priorities, and selection conditions.
SRCOrganize branches, execution, checkpoints, continuation, and reconciliation.
PythonPerform measurements, bounded computation, and mechanical state transport.

The editable conditional-tree document helps describe and review the intended structure. That Markdown view is separate from the executable SRC/DRM projection. A document change must reach the corresponding declarations and implementation before it can change runtime behavior. The conditional-tree source makes this promotion step explicit.

Layer responsibilitiesEditable tree and executable projection

Fine tuning through observed results

For SRA, fine tuning means refining the explicit system: clarifying a concept, narrowing an overgeneral condition, distinguishing causal variants, repairing a continuation, or improving an expensive computation. It is guided by the behavior the change produces.

Check whether the principle was selected, whether its premises were supported, and whether its use contributed to progress. Then vary the features that should be irrelevant and test a case where an essential condition is false. Review earlier cases that depend on the changed structure to detect regressions.

The migration design distinguishes a shared law, typed parameters, genuinely different causal variants, and compositions of existing principles. More general wording alone is insufficient. The abstraction must preserve the conditions that make its prediction or decision valid.

Generalization dimensions and causal variants

Two loops, with different kinds of change

During play, SRA can investigate an observation, propose an interpretation, test it, and revise the current knowledge. During development, the human and coding agent can change the reusable principles and mechanisms available to future runs. Keeping these loops distinct makes the origin of a new capability clear.

Human-Agent Principle Distillation also has a specific meaning here. Neural knowledge distillation trains a student model using a teacher model’s behavior. Yannick’s process extracts and integrates explicit principles. The coding assistance used to develop SRA is separate from the reasoning performed by SRA during play.
